old: Attention can temporarily hide those differences. CNBC's report on Nvidia's larger technology-fund weighting identifies prospective mechanical investor demand, which can affect trading independently of chip orders. That channel should remain distinct from operating growth. A company can enjoy supportive buying while facing a tougher earnings hurdle after its shares rise. Conversely, an operational improvement can deserve attention before broad fund flows turn favorable. The portfolio should be able to explain why a business is attractive even after a transient technical catalyst passes. [[n2087]]
new: Attention can temporarily hide the difference between trading support and operating growth. Portfolio implementation can create mechanical buying independently of chip orders, affecting near-term prices without changing customer demand. A company can enjoy that support while facing a tougher earnings hurdle after its shares rise. Conversely, an operational improvement can deserve attention before broad fund flows turn favorable. The portfolio should remain attractive after a transient technical catalyst passes, with valuation supported by customers and cash rather than an assumption of continuing mechanical purchases.
